resultText:
I found 12 problems in the watering change and wrote them to `out/findings.json`, which parses as valid JSON. Six I saw happen in the running app, mostly by calling the API with curl or loading the server-rendered page HTML. The other six come from reading the code only. There was no browser, so I couldn't check layout, clicks or hung requests directly.

**Seen in the running app:**
- **Server errors (500) on bad input:** a very large bed id sent to `POST /api/waterings`, `GET /api/waterings?bed_id=…` or `DELETE /api/waterings/{id}` returns 500 instead of a 4xx. So do `NaN` or `Infinity` sent as the litres value. (medium for the large id, low for NaN)
- **Duplicate waterings:** sending the same "Water now" request twice creates two rows with the same timestamp. A user who retries after a timeout or a lost response gets a double entry. (medium)
- **Tiny amounts shown as "0 L":** an amount like 0.001 litres is accepted, but the list and the success message show "0 L". (low)
- **Year-0001 dates accepted:** they are saved and listed as "1 Jan 1". (low)
- **Technical error text:** opening `/waterings?bed=abc` shows "Query.bed id: Input should be a valid integer…" and leaves the bed filter blank. (low)

**Suspected from the code:**
- **No retry when loading fails:** the dashboard's "Recent waterings" section and the waterings page show an error but offer no way to try again. On the dashboard the only fix is reloading the page. (medium)
- **Silent failure of the bed list on the waterings page:** if loading the beds fails, no error appears and the filter offers only "All beds". (medium)
- **No 10-second timeout:** if the server hangs, the "Watering…" or "Saving…" button stays disabled indefinitely. (medium)
- **Buttons re-enabled too early:** one shared "busy" marker covers every bed. Clicking "Water now" on one bed and then another re-enables the second button while its request is still pending, so a second click can record a duplicate. (low)
- **Time zone mismatch on "today":** the form takes today's date from the browser, but the server checks it against its own clock. A user in a time zone ahead of the server can be told today's date is "in the future". (low)
- **Long bed names at 375 px:** the stylesheet has no rule to wrap long words, so a long bed name with no spaces will likely push the watering tables wider than a phone screen. (low)

My testing added watering entries 3 to 6 on "North bed", including the year-0001 entry and the near-zero amount. They are still in the sample data.
